newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S. AFRICAN LEGISLATORS APPROVE CONSTITUTION.
newsitem.headline: S. AFRICAN LEGISLATORS APPROVE CONSTITUTION.

text.p: South African constitutional negotiators on Monday adopted a package of amendments that could see the country's post-apartheid constitution implemented on January 1.
"The job is done," Constitutional Assembly chairman Cyril Ramaphosa told Reuters after a committee of negotiators had approved agreements presented by two specialist sub-committees.
"On Friday we adopt the constitution, which is a formality, and we send it back to the Constitutional Court," he said.
The Constitutional Court referred a draft text adopted in May back to negotiators last month, calling for further refinement or more detail on eight issues.

The Constitutional Committee, comprising all the negotiators from the six political parties that have worked on the draft text, approved amendments on issues ranging from labour relations to the independence of the auditor general.
"I think we've done it...hopefully the Constitutional Court will agree to what we have decided here," said chief National Party negotiator Roelf Meyer.
The package included a revised labour relations clause which recognises the rights of individual employers to engage in collective bargaining without entrenching the right to lock out strikers.

"It appears to be a reasonably balanced formulation which reflects the realities of our industrial relations system," the Congress of South African Trade Unions, Cosatu, said in a statement afterwards.

"We welcome the fact that the Constitutional Committee has rejected attempts to bring the lock-out in through the back door and has rejected the introduction of the concept of economic power and collective action into the clause on collective bargaining," Cosatu said.
Ramaphosa said the amendments would be put to the full 490-member Constitutional Assembly on Friday and would then be submitted to the Constitutional Court for ratification.
If the text is approved by the court, it is likely to be implemented from January 1.
